text:
jordan: Heads up — p99 for /v1/chat/generate jumped ~2x after we ramped the blue->green runtime split to 60% around 09:12 UTC. Not customer-wide but heavy on chat and long-seq traffic. @tess @liam can you look?

tess: On it. Which runtime build did we roll? Any identifed cohorts or tenant IDs?

jordan: Runtime r5.5 (kernel selector + kv-cache changes). Affected cohort seems to be long prompt path (>512 tokens) and a few high-concurrency tenants. Sample trace id: trace-7f9a2c. Support already got an escalate from acme-corp.

liam: I pulled p95/p99 graphs — canary (10%) looked fine, spike appears when traffic passed 45% and sustained after 55%. Canary windows had lower seq mix.

anita: Possible regression around the late-binding scheduler tweak in r5.5. I saw one kernel fallback loop in nodes' logs earlier. Pasting a snippet: ```
2026-03-17T09:15:23Z WARN kernel_selector: fallback to slow-kernel for model xlm-2-large seq_len=768
2026-03-17T09:15:23Z INFO kv_cache: miss count spike=1.2k
```

sam: support-bot: ticket #SF-12345 (Acme) created and linked. Customer sees median fine but p99 ~1.8s -> 3.7s for chat completion. They provided a request id list: req-88a1, req-88a5.

jordan: Repro attempt: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input": "<large prompt>", "max_tokens":1500}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate -v --trace-id trace-7f9a2c (this hits the slow path reliably from our region vm-us-east-1a).

liam: Trying repro locally against canary and prod split. Canary at 10% still fine; when I hit the current green pool directly (r5.5) with 20 concurrent long requests I reproduce 2.5-3x p99 increase. Stack traces show kernel selection thrash + increased GC in python worker.

anita: Quick mitigation options: 1) Rollback runtime to r5.4 on green 2) Toggle runtime feature flag "late_binding_v2"=off for green 3) Route affected tenants back to blue (r5.4) via routing override. Which do we want now?

jordan: Prioritize least blast: route acme-corp and top 10 noisy tenants back to blue immediately. If spike persists, manual rollback of green. Liam can you prepare a traffic-split override?

liam: I'll push a route override for tenant ids [acme-*, beta-tenant-3, internal-loadtest*] to blue now. Pushing as: ```
redwood routing apply --tenant-pattern acme-* --target blue --until 2026-03-17T12:00:00Z --reason "p99 regression investigation"
```

support-bot: Routing override applied for 11 tenants. Notified support.

anita: While that's rolling, I'll start a bisection on the runtime change set between r5.4 -> r5.5. Suspect commits: 0a1b2c3 (scheduler tweak) and 4d5e6f7 (kernel-selector fallthrough). Running binary search across nodes; will instrument kernel_selector debug logging.

tess: Also enable fastpath kernel on green nodes as temporary band-aid: `runtime-config set green fastpath=true` — this reduced p99 in my quick lab test earlier. Is that safe?

anita: Fastpath flips on is OK for 2 hours; keep monitoring. Doing that now on a subset (50%) of green to avoid hidden correctness issues.

jordan: After overrides + fastpath, p99 dropped ~20% but still above baseline for some traffic. Good sign. Continue bisect. Also flag we may need a hotfix if bisect points to kernel selector.

liam: Bisection progress: after disabling commit 4d5e6f7 on a single node pool, p99 returned to baseline in that pool. Re-enabled elsewhere to confirm correlation.

anita: Confirmed — 4d5e6f7 (kernel-selector fallthrough) is culprit. Reproduces with long sequences and high concurrency. Creating hotpatch branch to fix the fallback loop and add an aggressive backoff to avoid thrash.

jordan: Great catch. Action items: anita -> hotpatch PR + canary patch; liam -> keep routing overrides until patch lands; tess -> coordinate customer comms and update ticket SF-12345; sam -> monitor alerts and close if stable.

tess: Contacted Acme support with workaround summary and ETA ~2 hours for patch. They asked for a temporary SLA note; I added a reduced-traffic workaround for them.

support-bot: Ticket SF-12345 updated: workaround applied, awaiting patch.

anita: PR opened 0f7e9a3 -> fixes fallback loop, adds metrics and a graceful degrade path. Kicking canary patch to green (5% first).

liam: Monitoring canary patch — initial 5% shows p99 back to baseline. If stable for 15m, we roll to 50% and then full.

jordan: Thanks team. Leaving this thread open until full rollout completes and support confirms with Acme. Will update SLO incident doc after closure.
